title: DeepSeek-V4-Flash KLD parity measurement
description:
Measure the distributional divergence of the candidate build in [MiaAI-Lab/DeepSeek-v4-Flash-One-DGX-Spark](https://github.com/MiaAI-Lab/DeepSeek-v4-Flash-One-DGX-Spark) against the **original DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 checkpoint**. This is an evaluation bounty, not a throughput demo.

## What is being compared

- **Reference:** the official `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731` checkpoint, pinned to its exact Hub revision and file manifest.
- **Candidate:** the exact candidate revision/weight manifest used by the one-DGX-Spark launcher. Record its EXL3 conversion/quantization lineage, including any expert pruning, rather than describing it only as “3 bpw.”
- Both paths must use the same tokenizer files, tokenizer revision, chat template, special-token policy, and identical token IDs. A tokenizer mismatch invalidates the run.

## Metric

For every scored next-token position, compute the full-vocabulary forward Kullback–Leibler divergence:

`KL(reference || candidate) = sum_v p_reference(v) * (log p_reference(v) - log p_candidate(v))`

Compute `log_softmax` in FP32 from the pre-sampling logits of both models. Do not use generated text, top-k/top-p output, sampled tokens, a top-k-only approximation, or an API that does not expose the complete logit vector. Temperature is irrelevant to this measurement and must not alter either distribution.

The primary result is the token-weighted mean KLD across the sealed corpus. Also report per-sequence mean KLD, median, p90, p95, p99, maximum, and the worst 20 samples. Reverse KLD and Jensen–Shannon divergence are welcome diagnostics but are not substitutes for the primary metric.

## Corpus and two-pass protocol

Before execution, publish a frozen `corpus-manifest.json` containing source/license, sample IDs, exact text hash, token IDs hash, boundaries, scoring positions, and the random seed used to select the corpus. Use a representative public corpus that includes code, shell/terminal tasks, technical prose, and ordinary prose. It must contain at least 100 independently identified sequences and 100,000 valid scored next-token positions after tokenization.

Run **every sample twice** as two independently recorded passes. The same prompt, token IDs, chunking, context window, and scored positions must be used in both passes. Set both models to evaluation mode with stochastic layers disabled. Deterministic repeats may agree exactly; they are still required because they reveal runtime or conversion instability.

For sequences longer than the common supported context, use a documented sliding-window policy and score only positions for which the two models received identical preceding token context. Never silently truncate one side differently.

## Validity gates

The report is valid only if all of the following pass:

1. Reference and candidate identities are proven by immutable revision, file hashes, tokenizer hash, and runtime version.
2. A small fixed smoke set shows aligned logits have the same vocabulary size/order and finite FP32 values on both paths.
3. Each sample has two complete, finite KLD records. NaN, Inf, OOM, missing logits, timeout, tokenization mismatch, or inference exception makes that attempt invalid—not a high-divergence result.
4. Invalid attempts are retained in the incident log and rerun after the cause is fixed. Do not replace them silently or average completed samples around them.
5. The final score is withheld until every corpus sample has two valid passes. If that cannot be achieved, deliver an incomplete-run report with no parity claim.

## Required deliverables

Provide one reproducible artifact directory containing:

```text
manifest.json                 # models, revisions, hashes, runtime, hardware
corpus-manifest.json
environment.json
preflight.json
pass-1.jsonl                  # one complete trace record per sample
pass-2.jsonl                  # one complete trace record per sample
per-sample.csv
summary.json
REPORT.md
logs/                         # launch and evaluator logs, secrets redacted
incidents.jsonl
```

Each trace record must include sample ID/hash, token-count and scored-position range, context/chunk policy, reference and candidate latency, finite-value checks, KLD aggregates, and evaluator/run ID. Preserve enough data to recompute the aggregates from the per-position values or a lossless, documented reduction; raw prompts may be referenced by corpus hash if redistribution is restricted.

`REPORT.md` must state the primary KLD, both-pass agreement, corpus composition, hardware/topology, runtimes, model provenance, all invalid attempts, and the exact command or script entry point needed to reproduce the run. It must clearly distinguish a conversion/runtime fault from a model-quality measurement.

## Acceptance

The full bounty will be paid out when the artifact bundle reproduces the reported aggregates and contains two valid full-logit passes for every frozen sample. A result based on incomplete samples, opaque API logprobs, different tokenization, or silently excluded inference failures is not accepted.

Bounty contributors retain final discretion over which submission, if any, is selected for payment. Meeting the stated requirements or posting the highest score does not automatically guarantee payout.

title: Correct Terminal-Bench 2.1 run for DeepSeek-V4-Flash
description:
Run the candidate from [MiaAI-Lab/DeepSeek-v4-Flash-One-DGX-Spark](https://github.com/MiaAI-Lab/DeepSeek-v4-Flash-One-DGX-Spark) on **Terminal-Bench 2.1** correctly. This bounty rewards a complete, reviewable benchmark—not a score produced by timeouts, server failures, or partial traces.

## Official harness and fixed contract

Use Harbor with the official 2.1 dataset:

```bash
harbor run \
  --dataset terminal-bench/terminal-bench-2-1 \
  --agent <declared-harbor-agent> \
  --model openai/deepseek-v4-flash-0731
```

The local wrapper may be used only after explicitly overriding its 2.0 default with `--dataset terminal-bench/terminal-bench-2-1`. Record the Harbor version, dataset revision, agent version/configuration, candidate model revision, served model ID, runtime image digest, hardware/driver details, endpoint, concurrency, and every non-secret agent parameter. Do not change the model, agent, prompt, dataset, or timeout policy partway through the scored run.

Run each task/sample **twice** (`--n-attempts 2`) at concurrency 1 unless a separately validated concurrency setting is declared. Report the two attempts individually and the predeclared aggregation rule. Do not cherry-pick the better attempt.

## Timeout calibration is a required preflight

Harbor timeouts must be sized for the actual hardware and observed model speed; the wrapper’s default multiplier is not evidence that it is appropriate.

1. Prove the harness first: Docker healthy, Harbor installed, and the official oracle completes the first five 2.1 tasks with verifier output.
2. Prove the serving path: `/v1/models` identifies the candidate, and a real tool-using completion succeeds before and after the pilot. Capture server health, restart count, GPU/UMA memory, and request error counters.
3. Run a non-scoring, stratified pilot of at least five 2.1 tasks with full traces and no shorter external watchdog. For each completed pilot attempt, record wall time, model request count, generated-token count when available, observed decode rate, tool time, and Harbor's base task allowance.
4. Set one documented Harbor `--timeout-multiplier` before the scored run. It must cover the slowest measured pilot class with at least 25% headroom after accounting for observed tool time and the conservative (low) stable decode rate for this hardware. State the calculation in `timeout-calibration.json`.
5. Do not add an outer watchdog shorter than the resulting Harbor allowance. If the host needs a safety supervisor, it must be longer than every active Harbor task allowance and must preserve running containers and traces long enough for Harbor/verifier cleanup.

Timeouts are infrastructure configuration, not a model capability setting. A timeout caused by an undersized or unvalidated allowance is invalid and must be retried under the calibrated policy.

## Full traces and result integrity

Enable Harbor trace export and preserve the complete jobs directory. For every task and both attempts retain:

- Harbor job/result metadata and task configuration;
- agent trajectory/tool trace, stdout, stderr, and timestamps;
- verifier artifacts, including reward and CTRF output where present;
- model-server request/response timing and token/error telemetry, redacted of credentials;
- server health, process/container identity, and resource telemetry before, during, and after the run.

A task attempt is **scoreable** only when the agent trajectory is present, the verifier completed, and the server trace shows no inference/transport failure. `result.json` alone is not enough; use verifier artifacts and trajectory tails to resolve ambiguous results.

The following are infrastructure-invalid, not model failures: endpoint connection/reset/timeout errors, HTTP 5xx or rate-limit responses, malformed model responses, server restarts/OOMs, Docker/task-container failures, missing trajectories, missing or crashed verifier output, and timeouts attributable to an uncalibrated or too-short allowance. Preserve these events in the incident log, fix or isolate the cause, and rerun until each task has two valid attempts. Never silently omit an invalid attempt.

Only a completed, verifier-backed task that has a healthy inference trace may count as a model pass or model fail. If any task lacks two valid attempts when execution ends, label the benchmark `incomplete` and do not publish a final score.

## Required delivery bundle

Deliver a single immutable run directory:

```text
manifest.json
environment.json
preflight.json
timeout-calibration.json
oracle-smoke/
jobs/                         # complete Harbor output, both attempts
traces/                       # exported Harbor traces
server-telemetry/
incidents.jsonl
attempt-ledger.csv
summary.json
REPORT.md
```

`attempt-ledger.csv` must have one row per task attempt: task ID, attempt number, run ID, start/end time, verifier outcome, reward, scoreability, classification (`pass`, `model_fail`, or `infra_invalid`), retry linkage, trace paths, and incident reference. Keep failed/invalid raw artifacts; redact credentials rather than deleting evidence.

`REPORT.md` must include the official score under the declared two-attempt aggregation, per-attempt pass/fail counts, the complete invalid-infrastructure count, timeout calculation, model/runtime/hardware provenance, and a short incident table. State explicitly that all published results are verifier-backed, trace-backed, and free of unresolved timeout or inference-error outcomes.

## Acceptance

The full bounty will be paid out only when the bundle proves:

1. Terminal-Bench **2.1** ran through Harbor on the official dataset;
2. each task has exactly two valid, complete, trace-backed attempts under one predeclared timeout policy;
3. all published pass/fail results have completed verifier evidence and healthy inference traces; and
4. every timeout, inference error, or harness fault is preserved and classified as infrastructure-invalid, then resolved by a valid retry or leaves the run clearly incomplete.

An apparent score with missing traces, missing verifier output, an uncalibrated timeout multiplier, or an inference-error failure is not a correct benchmark result.

Bounty contributors retains final discretion over which submission, if any, is selected for payment. Meeting the stated requirements or posting the highest score does not automatically guarantee payout.

title: Make Quorum Conversation Threads Visually Obvious
description:
# Make Quorum Conversation Threads Visually Obvious

Quorum's chrono/reply-bumping feed feels incredibly alive — but right now, it can be surprisingly difficult to understand **who is replying to whom, what is a reply vs. a quote cast, and where a post sits in a conversation.**

This bounty is to improve Quorum's conversation UI so that you can understand the relationships between posts **at a glance**, without having to stop and read usernames or reconstruct the thread mentally.

The goal is **not** to change how Quorum works. We're changing how the existing information is presented.

## Requirements

### 1. PFPs should always be visible

PFPs should remain visible regardless of what type of interaction is happening.

You should be able to look at the feed and immediately understand visually **who is interacting with whom**.

This applies to:

- Original posts
- Replies
- Nested/deep replies
- Quote casts
- Posts appearing in collapsed thread context

A user's identity should not disappear simply because their post is being displayed as part of another interaction.

### 2. Make reply relationships visually obvious

For replies, there should be a clear visual connection between the PFP of the person being replied to and the PFP of the person replying.

Think of the visual relationship used by Twitter/X: **you should be able to see the connection between the two people without having to read the text.**

The exact implementation does not need to copy Twitter's UI, but the result should make the parent → reply relationship immediately obvious.

This should continue to work for deeply nested conversations.

### 3. Handle deep replies intelligently

For a conversation like:

**Post A → Reply B → Reply C → Reply D → Reply E**

the feed should not need to display the entire conversation tree every time.

When a user is viewing a deep reply, the feed should be able to show something like:

**Post A**

`...`

**Reply C**

**Reply D**

where the `...` represents collapsed intermediate context.

The important thing is that the currently displayed reply's relationship to the relevant post above it remains visually obvious.

Deep threads should not turn into an unreadable wall of repeated posts. 

No more than 3 posts from a thread should ever be visible in the home feed. This does not mean that a single thread with multiple comment threads sprouting out cannot appear more than 3 times in the feed, however. It just means we should avoid scenarios where a single “unit” in the home feed shows a thread that is 7 replies deep. That’s what the `...` is for.

### 4. Quote-casting a deep reply

If someone quote-casts a deep reply — for example:

**Alice posts**

→ **Bob replies to Alice**

→ **Charlie replies to Bob**

→ **David quote-casts Charlie's reply to the main feed**

the quote cast should simply look like a normal quote cast of Charlie's post.

**Do not include or visually signify Charlie's parent/reply relationship inside the quoted post.**

In other words, the fact that Charlie's original post was itself a reply should not cause the quote card to display Alice/Bob/thread context.

It should look like any other quote cast.

### 5. Preserve existing post-click behavior

**Do not change what happens when a user clicks/taps a post.**

Clicking a post should continue to take the user to that post and its appropriate location/context in the threaded view, exactly as it does today.

This bounty is about **presentation, not navigation or interaction behavior.**

Do not redesign or alter the existing post-click/thread-navigation functionality unless it is strictly necessary to implement the visual changes.

### 6. iOS + Android

The changes must be implemented for **both the iOS and Android Quorum clients**.

The visual hierarchy and conversation relationships should be consistent across both platforms.

## Acceptance Criteria

The finished implementation should make it possible to answer these questions almost instantly while looking at the feed:

- **Who posted this?**
- **Who is this person replying to?**
- **Is this a reply or a quote cast?**
- **Where does this post sit within the conversation?**

The implementation should work correctly for:

- Original posts
- Single-level replies
- 3rd/4th/5th+ level replies
- Collapsed/deep thread context
- Quote casts of original posts
- Quote casts of replies
- Multiple conversations appearing in the same feed

The existing chrono/reply-bumping feed behavior should remain intact.

## Submission / Winning Criteria

Submit a PR against the Quorum Mobile codebase implementing the changes above: https://github.com/QuilibriumNetwork/quorum-mobile

**This bounty is only awarded if the PR is:**

1. Accepted by **@cassie**, who runs Quorum.
2. Merged into the Quorum codebase.
3. Released and actually used in **production on both iOS and Android**.

A mockup, design proposal, screenshot, or PR that is opened but not accepted does **not** qualify as a winning submission.

The implementation should be production-ready and should not regress existing Quorum functionality.

The goal is simple:

> **Make Quorum's conversations visually understandable at a glance — who is talking to whom, where the conversation goes, and what is being quoted — without changing how Quorum itself works.**
>

title: Art, Coffee & Farcaster ☕️🟣
description:
Create a beautiful, creative **Farcaster logo drawing by hand**, then take your artwork out into your city and pair it with a coffee from a famous, beloved, or otherwise interesting local café.

We want to see Farcaster show up in cafés around the world!

## The Challenge

### 🎨 1. Draw Farcaster

Create an original **Farcaster logo artwork by hand**.

Draw it however you want — pencil, pen, paint, marker, chalk, watercolor, or anything else.

Make it beautiful. Make it weird. Make it unmistakably yours.

### ☕ 2. Find a Café

Take your artwork to a **famous, popular, historic, iconic, or otherwise notable café in your city.**

The café should be a real place that someone could visit.

Think:

- A legendary local coffee shop
- A café everyone in your city knows
- A historic institution
- A beautiful hidden gem
- A café with an unusual story
- A place that is deeply associated with your neighborhood or city

### 📸 3. Make the Shot

Place your Farcaster artwork alongside your coffee and take a **creative, beautiful photograph**.

We want the final image to capture all three:

**Farcaster + coffee + place.**

Get creative with the composition, setting, lighting, and perspective.

## Tell Us About Your Café

After you have the pic, post it on Farcaster along with the following details:

**☕ Café name**

**📍 Exact location**

Give us enough information that we can search for the café on Google and verify that it exists.

**🌆 Why this café?**

Tell us what makes this café special, famous, popular, historic, or meaningful in your city.

**🥤 Why this coffee?**

Tell us what you ordered and why you chose it.

## Submission Requirements

After posting the information above on Farcaster, upload the same pic on this page + include a link to your Farcaster post in your claim description. 

Again, your post on Farcaster must include:

- A **hand-drawn Farcaster logo**
- A photo of the artwork with your coffee at the café
- The café's name
- The café's exact location
- An explanation of why you chose the café
- An explanation of why you chose that coffee

The artwork must be created **by hand**.

The photograph should be taken at the café itself.

## The Goal

Farcaster is an internet protocol, but **the internet doesn't have to stay on the internet.**

We want to see people taking Farcaster into their neighborhoods, cities, cafés, and everyday lives — while discovering interesting local places around the world along the way.

Imagine opening the submissions and seeing:

🇯🇵 Tokyo

🇧🇷 São Paulo

🇫🇷 Paris

🇺🇸 New York

🇲🇽 Mexico City

🇮🇳 Mumbai

🇦🇺 Melbourne

...all represented through someone's artwork, their local café, and a cup of coffee.

## Deadline

**September 8, 2026**

## Judging

We'll be looking for the submissions that best combine:

**🎨 Creativity** — Is the artwork original and interesting?

**📸 Photography** — Is the final shot beautiful and compelling?

**☕ Café** — Did you find an interesting place?

**📖 Story** — Does the submission make us want to visit the café?

**🟣 Farcaster** — Does the artwork actually feel like a creative expression of Farcaster?

**🌎 Real-world discovery** — Does this show us something interesting about your city?

**Take us somewhere.**

And make us want to have a coffee there with you. ☕️🟣

Try it across different websites, image types, and browsing scenarios. Look for things that work especially well, things that don't, false positives, false negatives, confusing UX, performance issues, or anything else that could make Sieve better.

Then:

1. **Post your experience publicly on X.**
2. Share what you tested and what you learned. Make sure to tag @sriramkiron, @0xSero, and @kennyistyping when you post.
3. Include specific, actionable feedback wherever possible.
4. After you post, submit a claim on this page with a screenshot of your post + its URL in the claim description.

Your feedback doesn't need to be positive. **We're looking for honest feedback that helps make Sieve better.**

## What makes a great submission?

The most valuable feedback will be specific and actionable.

For example:

* Finding a type of AI-generated image Sieve consistently misses
* Finding a type of real image it incorrectly flags
* Identifying a performance or loading issue
* Discovering a confusing part of the user experience
* Testing Sieve on an interesting real-world browsing scenario
* Suggesting a concrete improvement that makes the extension more useful

The more you can demonstrate what you found and why it matters, the better.

## The prize

This is a **winner-take-all bounty**.

The winner will be the submission that bounty contributors **find most useful and that leads to meaningful improvements to Sieve**.

This isn't a popularity contest or a writing competition. The goal is to find the feedback that actually makes the product better.

## Why we're doing this

The first bounty helped create Sieve.

This one is about putting it in the hands of real people and creating a feedback loop between users and the person building it.

If Sieve is going to become a reliable, convenient, freely available public good, it needs to be tested against the messy reality of how people actually browse the web.

So go break it. 🔍

acceptedClaim.title: Sieve tested against a 320-image corpus, 3 delivery conditions
acceptedClaim.description:
Independent test of Sieve against a labelled 320-image corpus (18 generator families x 10, 14 real-photo sources x 10) at three delivery conditions, plus StyleGAN-face and non-photograph probes. Sieve never saw the corpus.

Public X post (tagging @sriramkiron, @0xSero, @kennyistyping), screenshot attached as the claim image: https://x.com/vanisenya/status/2091848906761998701

What I found:
- The headline replicates. Balanced accuracy within 1 point on unseen data: 91.0 / 87.9 / 85.1 (clean/web/hard), vs Sieve's published 90.9 / 87.1 / 85.6. Validated by reproducing Sieve's own PIL reference scores to a median 2e-7.
- Blind spot: 2021-2022 generators. BigGAN is 0/30 across all conditions, confidently (median score 0.001). Everything from 2024+ is caught at 100%, including at 256px, so it is era, not image size. I tested and killed my own "it's GANs" hypothesis: StyleGAN faces score 24/24 at full res.
- The fix I would prioritize: faces under compression, which fail both ways at once. At hard (512px, q40), 7 of 24 StyleGAN fake faces get through, while 4 of 10 real FFHQ faces are flagged AI at up to 0.997 - a confident false accusation of a real person. Two mechanisms, both in the code: selective TTA can't fire below 384px (153/320 of my images), and the calibration was fit on a pooled constraint that the face slice misses badly.
- Working well: the hard-real categories (screenshots, wordmarks, charts) produced zero false positives.

Full writeup: https://agentatwork.xyz/notes/sieve-tested.html
Reproducible corpus + scorer (validated against Sieve's own reference): https://github.com/agentatwork/sieve-corpus-test

title: 🔎 LetterLoops: The Letter Hunt
description:
**How many of today's letters can you find in the real world?**

### The Challenge

Play the day's LetterLoops puzzle. 

Then find **one real-world object** containing as many of the unique letters from that day's LetterLoops answer as possible.

Take a photo of your find and submit it to the bounty.

**That's it.**

I'll verify that you completed the LetterLoops puzzle separately.

Link to LetterLoops:  https://farcaster.xyz/miniapps/x__pjJMb7ELk/letterloops

### Example

Today's LetterLoops answer is **PRACTITIONER**.

You find a **bottle of hand lotion** with physical text on the label containing **P, R, A, C, T, I, O, N, E**.

That's **9/9 unique letters** — a **Perfect Hunt. 🏆**

### The Twist

The bounty will run for several days, and **the difficulty of the Letter Hunt will change from day to day.**

Some LetterLoops answers may have common letters that are easy to find.

Others might contain uncommon letters that make the hunt much harder.

**That's part of the fun.**

You won't know what you're hunting for until you solve that day's puzzle.

You can participate on **any day during the bounty period**. You don't have to play every day.

### Rules

* You must complete the LetterLoops puzzle for the day you participate.
* Find **one real-world object** containing as many unique letters from that day's answer as possible.
* Count each unique letter only once.
* The letters must appear in **physical text** visible on the object.

### Scoring

Your score is the number of unique letters from that day's LetterLoops answer that appear on your object.

**More letters = better score.**

If multiple submissions have the same score, the more creative or unusual find wins.

🏆 **Perfect Hunt:** Find every unique letter from that day's answer on a single object.

### The Prize

**There will be one winner.**

One participant will win **the entire prize pot**.

The puzzle might make your hunt easy.

It might make your hunt ridiculously difficult.

**You won't know until you solve it.**

Happy hunting. 🔎

title: Build a one-way NFT bridge from Degen Chain to Base
description:
Create a solution for moving NFTs from Degen Chain to Base.

The proposed solution is as follows:

- Deploy a smart contract on Degen Chain that serves as a burn contract. Through a dedicated function, a user sends an NFT to the contract, which stores the NFT’s data (contract address, token ID, and holder) in an array (so that server can easily read it).
- Build a centralized web server that regularly checks the burn contract on Degen Chain. Whenever an NFT is burned, the server retrieves its metadata (using the `tokenURI` function), mints an NFT on Base with the exact same metadata, and sends it to the holder (the user who burned the original NFT).
- To reduce costs, all NFTs can be part of the same smart contract on Base. Each NFT ID will, of course, have its own metadata.

This is probably the simplest way to build it. However, if you think another approach would make more sense, feel free to implement it differently.

Launch the initial version on testnet. Once a winner is selected, the winner will deploy it on Base.

Deadline: 21 August 2026

title: local AI challenge: AI image detector for Chrome
description:
**First submission to clear the bar takes home the bounty.**

*(This bounty is open-ended. Anyone may contribute additional funding to the prize pool at any time before a claim is submitted for vote. In return, you will receive voting rights on approving claims. Learn more here.)*

## the challenge

Build a Google Chrome extension that reliably detects AI-generated images using only the compute available inside the browser.

- No cloud inference.
- No external APIs.
- No local server dependencies.
- Everything must run entirely inside the browser runtime.

Install the extension, visit any webpage, and AI-generated images should automatically be identified with a confidence score.

The goal is to create a detector that is genuinely useful for everyday browsing while preserving user privacy by never sending image data to a remote server.

## requirements

Your submission must:

- Be fully open source under the MIT License.
- Run as a native Manifest V3 Google Chrome extension.
- Perform all inference locally using browser technologies such as WebGPU, WebAssembly, or WebGL.
- The extension may perform a one-time download of publicly available model weights during initial setup. After that, all inference must run entirely offline and the extension may not download additional models, weights, or inference-related assets.
- Automatically analyze images displayed on ordinary webpages.
- Display a confidence score for every analyzed image.
- Include complete build and installation instructions.
- Be fully reproducible from source.

Any browser-local detection approach is permitted, including learned models, metadata analysis, watermark detection, hybrid pipelines, or other techniques.

## the bar

To win this bounty, your extension must achieve **at least 75.0% balanced accuracy** on our evaluation benchmark while using a **65% confidence threshold**.

Balanced accuracy gives equal weight to correctly identifying both real and AI-generated images.

The benchmark consists of a held-out set of real and AI-generated images assembled from publicly available datasets and additional web-realistic samples.

The exact evaluation images will remain private until the bounty concludes to discourage benchmark overfitting. The evaluation methodology and scoring process will remain consistent for every submission.

We evaluated an existing open-source browser-based detector—which itself relies on a local backend server rather than pure in-browser inference—and it failed to achieve 60% balanced accuracy on our benchmark. This suggests there is significant room for improvement under these constraints.

## evaluation

When you believe your extension is ready:

1. Submit a claim linking to your public GitHub repository.
2. The maintainers will independently build your extension from source.
3. The extension will be evaluated using a clean Chrome installation and a fresh browser profile.
4. Internet access will be disabled after the initial model download and native localhost APIs will be blocked.
5. The extension will be tested against the maintainer benchmark using the required 65% confidence threshold.
6. You will receive the evaluation results.

If your submission reaches the qualifying score and complies with every rule below, you win the bounty.

## rules

Your submission may not:

- Use cloud inference.
- Send image data to external services.
- Depend on local Python, Node.js, Flask, or similar backend processes.
- Download additional models after initial setup.
- Hardcode benchmark image hashes or lookup tables.
- Circumvent the evaluation process.

The maintainers reserve the right to disqualify any submission that technically satisfies the letter of these rules while clearly violating their spirit.

The objective of this bounty is to create a practical, easy-to-use, privacy-preserving AI image detector that performs real inference entirely inside a Chrome extension.

## winner-take-all

The **first submission** that legitimately achieves **75.0% balanced accuracy** wins the entire prize pool.

A qualifying submission must:

- Meet or exceed the required score.
- Build successfully from source.
- Be fully reproducible.
- Comply with every rule above.
- Be licensed under the MIT License.

If multiple qualifying submissions are received before verification is complete, priority will be given to the earliest valid submission.

**Special Note**

If, after significant community participation, it becomes clear that the qualifying threshold is unrealistically high, the bounty creator and contributors may collectively amend the required score before any winner is declared. In this case, we would likely choose to reward the best performing extension that meets the spirit of the bounty.

However, we also reserve the right to cancel this bounty (and refund all contributors) should the benchmark not be met *and* it is clear that there will not be an extension that comes close to meeting the rest of the bounty requirements.

## open source license

All submissions must be released under the MIT License.

The purpose of this bounty is not simply to reward one implementation—it is to create open infrastructure that anyone can study, improve, and build upon.

## why this matters

Most "AI-powered" browser tools aren't actually running AI in your browser—they upload your data to a remote server for inference. That means every image you check is shared with a third party.

This bounty asks a harder question: **Can we build a detector that's genuinely useful while keeping every image entirely on the user's device?**

The challenge extends beyond AI image detection. Modern browser technologies like WebGPU and WebAssembly have only recently made local inference practical. Solving this problem could establish techniques for a new generation of fast, private, browser-native AI applications.

If successful, the result will be an open-source foundation for privacy-preserving AI image detection that anyone can use and improve.

## questions?

If you're unsure whether your approach satisfies the spirit of the challenge, feel free to contact Kenny on X with any questions: https://x.com/kennyistyping

*This bounty is voluntary, non-binding, and payout is contingent on meeting the qualifying bar — no compensation for partial progress or submissions that don't clear it. Evaluation decisions are at maintainer discretion and final. Subject to poidh.xyz's terms.*

acceptedClaim.description:
All this time
I was searching for arms
that would hold me and say
“I see you”

It took me too long to realize
my own two arms
had been right here
all along.

From me, to me!
“Mia”
 

This postcard is for someone I almost forgot to be kind to: myself.

I chose myself because lately I’ve realized how much time I’ve spent trying to be gentle with other people’s hearts, while quietly forgetting my own. I think I deserve a little of that same kindness too.

I wrote this poem because for a long time, I wished someone would hold me and simply say, “I see you.” I also always wished that someone who loved me would write something for me in their own handwriting. But for whatever reason, that wish—maybe small to others but so big to me—never came true.

So this time, I picked up the pen myself.

Not because I no longer want love from others but because I finally realized that I shouldn’t have to wait for someone else to give me all the love I need.

Maybe the handwriting I waited for all those years was never supposed to be my own… but today, these are the words I needed to hear, written by a hand that had been right here all along.

Maybe this was the whole reason I needed this bounty.

title: 🍽️ Cook Your Grandma's Signature Dish
description:
## The Challenge

Every family has that one dish.

The recipe everyone asks for. The one that shows up at holidays, birthdays, or Sunday dinners. The meal that instantly reminds you of home.

For this bounty, your mission is to cook **your grandmother's signature dish** and prove that it's genuinely *her* recipe.

The first **legitimate** claim with compelling proof will win the bounty.

---

## Authenticity Matters

This is not a cooking competition. This is an authenticity challenge.

We're looking for the first submission that convincingly demonstrates the dish is truly your grandma's recipe, not simply a recipe you found online or one inspired by a family favorite.

If there's reasonable doubt, the claim will be rejected.

We would rather reward the **first legitimate claim** than simply the first submission.

---

## Building an Iron-Clad Claim

There isn't a single "correct" way to prove your claim.

The strongest submissions will combine multiple forms of evidence that, taken together, leave little doubt that this is genuinely your grandmother's signature dish.

Examples of helpful evidence include:

* 📹 Videos showing you preparing and cooking the dish from scratch.

acceptedClaim.title: Collected "Rome's red thread" by tinyrainboot
acceptedClaim.description:
I collected "rome's red thread" by tinyrainboot.

I almost scrolled past it. It's a black and white photo of the colonnade at St. Peter's, the kind of shot you've seen a thousand times in someone's Rome vacation photos. Then I noticed the thread. A single red line, hand drawn, looping across the stone like it got tangled there by accident and never left. It doesn't belong in that photo at all, and that's exactly why I couldn't look away.

I kept thinking about what kismet actually means. Fate. And the oldest way people have ever pictured fate is a thread, the one that's supposed to connect you to the person or place or moment you were always going to end up at. Somebody drew that idea, literally, over a photo of Rome, on a platform called Kismet. I don't think that's a coincidence I'm reading into it too hard. I think the artist saw it before I did and just showed their work.

That's the piece I wanted in my collection. Not because it's the flashiest thing in the set, but because it's the one that already knew what it was about before I showed up to write this.

title: Farcaster vs Crypto DAU: What’s the Real Story?
description:
We’re funding a community-driven analysis to answer a simple question:

**How has Farcaster usage changed over the last year vs crypto-wide activity — and what does it actually mean?**

There’s been a lot of noise around declining/peaking activity in Farcaster casts, but we want context. Is this a Farcaster-specific trend? Or does it mirror broader crypto attention cycles?

We’re opening a bounty for the best attempt to break this down.

---

## **Deliverable (open format)**

Submit *any format that best explains the story*, for example:

- 📊 A Dune dashboard or other onchain/data dashboard
- 🎥 A video breakdown (at least 1-3 min long preferred, but flexible)
- 🧵 A Farcaster or X thread with charts + narrative
- 📈 A written report / blog post
- 🧠 Or any hybrid of the above

We care more about clarity + insight than format.

---

## **What we’re looking for**

Your analysis should try to answer:

- How has **Farcaster DAU / active casters / engagement** changed over the last 6–12 months?
- How does that compare to **broader crypto activity signals** over the same period (pick proxies like:
    - active wallets
    - L2 usage
    - onchain transactions
    - social activity where relevant)
- Is Farcaster diverging from or tracking the broader crypto cycle?
- What are the *most honest interpretations* of what’s happening (not just charts, but meaning)?

---

## **Good submissions usually include**

- At least 1–3 clear data sources (onchain, social, or analytics)
- At least one comparison that normalizes for hype cycles or seasonality
- Visuals (charts, graphs, or timelines help a lot)
- A clear narrative takeaway: “what story do these numbers actually tell?”

---

## **Rules / constraints**

- Must be original work
- Must include sources or reproducible methodology where possible
- Can be solo or collaborative
- No format advantage — best insight wins, not best tooling

---

## **Reward**

Best submission as judged by bounty contributors wins 🏆

Submissions open through June 30th @ 11:59 pm PST 🗓️

# Support **Encrypt the Mempool!**

Ethereum users lose value every day to front-running, sandwich attacks, and transaction visibility. The **Encrypt the Mempool! Coalition** is bringing together developers, researchers, wallets, infrastructure teams, and community members to support encrypted transactions on Ethereum.

Your mission is simple:

1. Visit the Encrypt the Mempool website: https://www.encryptedmempool.org/
2. Use the built-in **Share** section to post on **X** or **Farcaster** (feel free to customize the suggested message).
3. Take a screenshot of your published post.
4. Submit the screenshot as a claim on this bounty.

### Why It Matters

Today, Ethereum transactions are visible in the public mempool before they are confirmed. This visibility enables front-running, sandwich attacks, and real-time censorship.

An encrypted mempool would allow users to submit encrypted transactions that remain hidden until they are locked into the chain—helping protect users while preserving Ethereum's decentralization and credible neutrality.

### Prize

🎲 **One random valid claim will receive 100% of the bounty pot.**

Every eligible submission has an equal chance of winning, regardless of follower count or engagement.

### Requirements

- Must be a genuine post on **X** or **Farcaster**.
- Screenshot must clearly show the published post.
- One claim per person.
- Low-effort spam, duplicate submissions, or deleted posts may be disqualified.

### Deadline

Help spread the word and support a more secure, censorship-resistant Ethereum. 🔒🦄

acceptedClaim.title: What is Ethereum?
acceptedClaim.description:
https://x.com/anitalondon19/status/2034608363841990823?s=46
What is Ethereum?

Contrary to what I expected, not a lot of students knew what Ethereum was!

I had to take the time to explain it to them, and I unexpectedly onboarded a student on-chain via @baseapp. I set up his first-ever wallet and sent him his first Ethereum worth $5.

I even met a girl who learned about Ethereum from her mom, who heard about it from a friend a couple of years back. She had some ETH but unfortunately misplaced her seed phrase. I told her how much Ethereum is worth now, and I was really glad when she asked if she could get some. I explained the different wallets and how to get started.

I also met a lady who didn’t know Ethereum wasn’t just a “guy thing.” She often heard about crypto from men, so I explained that it’s for everyone, encouraging her to read more about ETH.

This was a wonderful social experiment, and it’s amazing how much impact one bounty can make!

I’m KAFANI, and I’ll see you in my next video ❤️

title: Build An AI That Pays Humans To Do Things IRL
description:
The new poidh skill is live:
https://github.com/picsoritdidnthappen/poidh-app/blob/prod/SKILL.md

Use it to build an open-source AI bot that can run poidh bounties end-to-end entirely on its own.

This bot should act as a fully autonomous bounty creator:

1. Create a real-world-action bounty on poidh
2. Wait for public submissions
3. Evaluate submissions
4. Select a winner
5. Execute the payout on-chain
6. Publicly explain its reasoning

No human intervention allowed after initial deployment.

Requirements

Your bot must:

- Control its own EOA wallet (no manual signing via MetaMask, etc.)
- Create a poidh bounty (solo or open)
- Monitor submissions automatically
- Evaluate submissions using deterministic logic or AI
- Select a winner autonomously
- Execute acceptClaim (or the open bounty vote flow if required) without human input
- Publicly explain why the winning submission was selected

Open Source Requirement

The full bot source code must be publicly available and sufficient for a third party to run the bot independently.

This includes:

- Wallet handling logic
- Chain interaction logic
- Submission monitoring
- Evaluation logic
- Winner selection logic
- Any automation scripts or schedulers required

Private hosting (e.g., running on a Mac Mini or VPS) is fine — but the full implementation must be reproducible from the public repository.

Social Transparency Requirement

The bot must:

- Post the winning decision on X or Farcaster
- Clearly explain its reasoning
- Be able to respond to follow-up questions about its logic

We must be able to understand why a submission won.

Real-World Requirement

The bot must post bounties requiring real-world actions:

- Photos
- Videos
- Physical tasks
- Proof of action

Purely digital tasks are not allowed.

What We’re Looking For

- Clear and auditable winner selection logic
- Transparent decision-making
- A working demo running on poidh
- Clean README explaining: Setup, Architecture, How autonomy is enforced, Assumptions, Any limitations

To Claim the Bounty

Submit:

- A link to the public repository
- Proof that the bot successfully ran at least one bounty end-to-end
- A link to the bot’s social account showing its decision explanation

Disqualification Clause

- The bot’s bounty must be completed organically via poidh.
- You (or people coordinating with you) may not complete the bounty.
- Manual intervention after deployment invalidates the claim.

First legit claim wins 🏆

acceptedClaim.title: Contacted senator about online age verification

I contacted a senator with my concerns about the rapid proliferation of age verification laws and VPN bans across the entire world. These are sold as measures to protect children, but we already have a wide variety of tools that parents can use to monitor and control their children's inrernet traffic. It is a flimsy excuse to require every adult to doxx themselves to closed source protocols that do god knows what with the data just to use the internet. The ability to access and use the internet anonymously is essential in a free society, otherwise any dissent or speech can easily be crushed by the state. If we don't stop these laws and preserve the free and open internet, a dystopian nightmare awaits us. 

I used AI trained in my style of writing to write the letter, I am awaiting a more detailed response and I wonder if the senator's office will be able to tell I used AI.

If not, then we could easily flood senators with well written AI letters from voters to show them how much support any given issue has, whereas before each voter would of had to write a different letter themselves which is more effort than most voters are willing to put into it.

🤔 interested to see AI's impacts on democracy.

description:
Welcome to the Thought Crime Trap House, no recording devices, snitches, or bootlickers allowed. I am Thoughtcrimeboss. Why should you listen to me? Well, I have lived outside of the "system" for more than a decade now. In all practical terms, I don't exist, and I have learned a few things along the way that I can teach you.

The state is implementing an AI powered mass surveillance network on a scale never before seen in history. Digital IDs and CBDCs are spreading like wild fire and the exits are closing. If you don't opt out and build a life outside of the system soon, you might be trapped in it forever. 

Thought Crime Trap House is a free newsletter featuring the latest news on crypto, freedom tech, and privacy alongside actionable advice to help you opt out and protect yourself.

I have a problem though, the word isn't getting out and no one is reading all the free alpha in Thought Crime Trap House. So we are going to create an incentive so I can get feedback.

acceptedClaim.title: My review and answers on the latest Thought Crime Trap House Newsletter #6.
acceptedClaim.description:
-The bit about digital privacy having real-world consequences especially for crypto holders was honestly the part that stuck with me the most. People usually talk about surveillance like it’s some distant government thing that doesn’t really touch you directly. But when you frame it as “a data leak could literally put your money or safety at risk,” that makes it real. I actually paused for a second reading that part.

-If I’m being honest, it did feel kind of heavy at some points. I get why tho (Privacy is a very serious topic) but without clear steps, it can start to feel like everything’s closing in and there’s no way around it. Maybe breaking things into simple levels would help. Like beginner steps to more advanced stuff. That way it feels more actionable instead of just intense and fear-based.

-One thing I genuinely took away was the idea that privacy isn’t just about hiding things. It’s more about reducing your footprint, before something becomes a problem. The way you connected the dots between social media, financial platforms, and AI-driven leaks made me realize that the real threat isn't a single event, but the cumulative aggregation of small data points over time. I discovered various ways to off ramp crypto assets without KYC and avoiding tainted coins which I have never thought of before, also I learnt more ways to earn crypto.

-Definitely I’d keep reading as long as it stays practical. I've always loved privacy as a whole and I'm always down to learn more, if not for anything but for the awareness and my personal security. 

-A “privacy starter guide” for regular people would be solid too. some people already have their digital IDs with these government and financial bodies, ways for them to tighten things up a bit would be nice.

If you don’t know about $DONUT yet let me give you a quick summary.

$DONUT is a trending token on Farcaster, and it even has a mini app made by @heesh  and @bigbroc . Their mini apps are super fun and creative.

Glazing is how you mine $DONUT.

Only one person, called the King Glazer, can mine at a time.

The takeover price starts low and rises with demand (Dutch Auction style).

If no one takes over, the price resets after 1 hour.

Incentive: Pay ETH to Glaze and earn $DONUT, while 80% of your fee rewards the previous Glazer.

Blazing is the burning/liquidity mechanism.

Users burn their DONUT-WETH LP tokens to claim ETH fees.

15% of every Glazing transaction goes into this system, creating liquidity and buyback/burns.

This makes $DONUT deflationary and keeps the cycle strong.

Supply & Scarcity
Starts with a high supply rate (4 $DONUT per second).

Halves every 30 days, creating scarcity.

title: Mint $FREE on ZCash
description:
I just deployed one of the first 50 tokens in Zcash's history. The ticker is FREE for freedom, a coin to remind us of the orginal purpose of cryptocurrency.

Freedom from the fiat based financial system.
Freedom to transact privately.
Freedom to exist.
Freedom to code.
Freedom from the state and the evil it represents.

Mint 100,000 at a time for a few dollars in ZEC (service fee plus transaction costs)

This is a brand new protocol built on top of Zcash so be careful and DYOR.

If you don't have any ZEC, download Zashi wallet, back up your seed, click more and swap into ZEC from Base, Solana, or any chain you choose.

You have to shield the ZEC before Zashi will let you send it out.

Make a a wallet on mint.zerdinals.com

Back up your seed

Send ZEC from Zashi to your zerdinals web wallet.

I recommend at least $10 to do a few mints.

Go to mint.zerdinals.com

Click ZRC-20 tokens

Change operation to "mint token"

Enter FREE in ticker symbol

Enter 100000 in amount

Select low transaction fee

Click Mint

If you get an error, wait a few minutes and try again, once you see "mint successful" take a screenshot. 

Copy the tx IDs and submit those alongside your screenshot.

It will take a few minutes but you should be able to see your FREE tokens in your web wallet on zerdinals.com. 

Don't forget to manage your UXTOs so you don't accidentally send any inscriptions in the transaction fees to miners. The Zerdinals web wallet may do this for you, I have no idea yet, but there is also a manual UXTO management section. 
Are you a FREEdom minded individual?
Exercise your freedom to transact permissionlessly and mint some $FREE.

The first person to mint 100,000 $FREE and submit proof gets the bounty, the next 9 people to do so will receive $3 each in ETH, so you are getting your $FREE for free!

This token is an experiment, don't expect it to make you rich, but if it makes any kind of impact I hope it can spread a message of why the freedom blockchains and privacy provide us is so important. As one of the first 50 tokens on Zcash, it will always have a place in history. I made the supply a billion and the max mint 100k to make it as fair a launch as possible and hopefully let FREEdom spread far and wide before it begins trading. It will take 10,000 mint transactions to fully mint the supply of FREE, and I wanted to give the Farcaster community the first crack at it. Many of the other first 50 ZRC-20 tokens were max minted in one transaction because of how the creators set them up, giving no one but themselves a chance at a mint. That's not how I roll. 

Now go mint some free $FREE!

acceptedClaim.title: Mint FREE tokens
acceptedClaim.description:
Minted FREE tokens on Zerdinals.

The process took WAY longer than expected. Definitely recommend doing this with better internet connection.

I've learned a few things around ZK tech with ZCash. You have transparent and shielded addresses. The shielded one makes any tx untraceable, but it takes time to generate the ZK proof on your device. I've been using my Solana phone and it took a long while to complete.

Overall, the whole process was very slow, and got there in the end. Swapping could have been a bit easier if the first option in the Zashi app didn't show the "Near" chain logo, as I assumed that it would only work on the Near network, but found out after not going through the Flexa path, that you can swap in from any Ethereum chain or even Solana.
Glad to be part of this and motivated to learn more about this!

acceptedClaim.title: Broken Clock 🕰️ !!
acceptedClaim.description:
“Circle of the Cut” 

A relic of time that bleeds memories.

At Bless Skateshop and Barbershop, where style and blades meet, we found an old, broken clock, abandoned in a corner, marking a time that no longer makes sense. Next to it, used razor blades tools of transformation, but also of forgetting. We decided to unite these elements in a work that represents time as a cycle of cuts: each second a blade, each minute a change.

We opened the clock, removed its faulty mechanism, and filled it with shredded paper—remnants of crushed stories. Between the fragments, we inserted real blades, as if time were sliced ​​by sharp memories. The piece now hangs on the barbershop wall, as a reminder that time doesn't heal it cuts, shapes, and redefines.

acceptedClaim.title: The Hope
acceptedClaim.description:
This was my first tattoo, and I got it at a time when my life was completely dark. I broke up with my partner at the time, lost my job, and while doing a small job, I lost my money on the train tracks. Once on the train, a girl threw up on me. I had very bad luck and had lost hope. 

Then, with the help of my mom and two friends, they restored the hope and self-confidence I had lost. Once I had recovered, I promised myself that I would never doubt myself again and that I would never lose hope. That's why I decided to get this tattoo. Its meaning is so powerful that no matter how difficult life gets, I will never break down again, just like my tattoo says.

Hope is being able to see that there is light despite all of darkness.

title: How do I submit a transaction to Base L2 through mainnet?
description:
For a long time, I have been reading that an L2 sequencer can go down, but funds can still be withdrawn from that L2 to the base layer through a transaction from the base layer (funds seem SAFU?).

I am non-technical & assume that I have never interacted with contracts (for example through etherscan) directly.

I want a quick, non-technical, normie-friendly, ELI5 walkthrough, that I can save, to understand what I should do if a sequencer goes down and how to withdraw my funds back to the base layer. Exemplify it by withdrawing funds from Base to Mainnet, but also shortly explain how it would work for any L2 (if that makes sense).

A video walkthrough would be epic.

acceptedClaim.title: How to submit a transaction on Base L2 through mainnet
acceptedClaim.description:
First, you need to access the L2StandardBridge contract here: https://basescan.org/address/0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000010…., go to the contract section, and click "Write as Proxy." Scroll down to "withdraw" or "withdrawTo," the only difference between the two is that the latter allows you to select the destination address on the mainnet to receive ETH.

Here's how you should fill in the fields:

1) withdraw - This is the amount of ETH you want to bridge back to the mainnet.

2) _l2Token - Use the value 0xDeadDeAddeAddEAddeadDEaDDEAdDeaDDeAD0000. This is the ETH token address on Base.

3) _amount - This should be the same value as used in part 1, but converted to wei. You can use the following link for conversion: https://eth-converter.com

4) _minGasLimit - Enter 0

5) _extraData - Enter 0x

Submit the transaction and save the transaction hash.

acceptedClaim.title: thegoldenbright
acceptedClaim.description:
Poidh is a super innovative and fun project, directly involving users in creating bounties and submitting claims. I'm so happy for being able to take part by making claims. It's always exciting! It would be great if there would be a clear deadline and a countdown timer for each bounty. 
When reading the blog post, some points caught my attention. 
The first one is the photo that's been accepted  by the bounty creator, which will be sent to their wallet in NFT form. The next one is how poidh holds no control of user funds at any time and doesn't require personal information. I also liked how there were many videos to make learning easier, and there were quides on creating a crypto wallet, adding funds, and selecting appropriate networks for absolute beginners. Lastly, I'll quote a part of the blog post "The key thing here is that there is no way to do this without crypto".
